info.title: MoEngage Campaign Stats and Reports API
info.description:
The Stats API allows you to fetch detailed campaign stats synchronized in real time. 
The Campaign Report API allows you to download campaign reports for any specific date range.

dc.description: The ‘dc’ in the API Endpoint URL refers to the MoEngage Data Center (DC). MoEngage hosts each customer in a different DC. You can find your DC number and replace the value of ‘dc’ in the URL by referring to the DC and API endpoint mapping [here](/api/introduction#data-centers). Your MoEngage Data Center (DC) can be 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, or 101.

post.description: This API fetches data at the platform level and provides data for all types of campaigns.

x-mint.content:
#### Rate Limit

This API provides all version stats, and the call rate is limited to **100 API calls per minute** per workspace.
<Info>
 - Make sure to pass the relevant Campaign IDs in the request to fetch stats for flow-linked campaigns.
 - Stats data is retained for the entire lifetime of a campaign, from its start date, there is no fixed retention cutoff. The 30-day limit applies only to the date range of a single API call, not to how far back you can query.
</Info>

parameters.name: MOE-APPKEY
parameters.description: This is the Workspace ID of your MoEngage account that must be passed with the request. You can find it in the MoEngage dashboard at **Settings** > **Account** > **APIs** > **Workspace ID (earlier app id)**.

400.description:
**Bad request**
Possible issues include duplicates, invalid data types, or missing mandatory attributes.

401.description:
**Unauthorized**
This response is returned upon unauthorized request. Provide appropriate authentication credentials.

403.description:
**Forbidden**
This response is returned when our account does not have access to the campaign stats management features.

429.description:
**Too many requests**
This response is returned when the number of requests per minute has exceeded the rate limit.

500.description:
**Internal server error**
This response is returned when the system runs into an unexpected error.

example.description: An unexpected error was encountered while processing this request. Please contact MoEngage Team

get.description: This API downloads campaign reports for any specific date range. You can fetch reports for one-time and periodic campaigns.

x-mint.content:
#### Limits

- **Expiry**: The generated reports will expire in **7 days** from the date of creation.
- **Max Range**: You can generate reports for up to **90 days**.

#### Generating the Signature
A unique signature must be passed in the headers to verify the caller's authenticity. 

The signature is `SHA256(Api_ID + "|" + FILENAME + "|" + SECRET_KEY)`.

```python
# SAMPLE IMPLEMENTATION IN PYTHON
from hashlib import sha256
Api_ID = "YOUR-APP-ID"
FILENAME = "Report_-_test_20210217.zip"
SECRET_KEY = "YOUR-SECRET-KEY"
Signature_Key = Api_ID + "|" + FILENAME + "|" + SECRET_KEY
# Now Signature is hexdigest of sha256 of Signature_Key
Signature = sha256(Signature_Key.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
```

parameters.name: APP_ID
parameters.description: This is the Workspace ID of your MoEngage account that must be passed with the request. You can find it in the MoEngage dashboard at **Settings** > **Account** > **APIs** > **Workspace ID (earlier app id)**.

parameters.name: FILENAME
parameters.description:
The name of the report file to download. It is a combination of report name, generation date, and file format.
Example: `Report_test_20210217.zip`

parameters.name: Signature
parameters.description: A custom signature generated by SHA256(Api_ID + "|" + FILENAME + "|" + SECRET_KEY).

200.description: Successful API request automatically downloads the report file.

400.description:
**Bad Request**
Reasons: Invalid Report file name, requested report is older than 7 days, or incorrect App Id.

401.description: Unauthorized. Invalid Signature or Signature Missing.

basicAuth.description:
Authentication is done via Basic Auth. This requires a base64-encoded string of your credentials in the format 'username:password'.

- **Username**: Use your MoEngage workspace ID (also known as the App ID). You can find it in the MoEngage dashboard at **Settings** > **Account** > **APIs** > **Workspace ID (earlier app id)**.
- **Password**: Use your API Key, which you can find within the **Campaign report/Business events/Custom templates/Catalog API/Inform Report** tile.

For more information on authentication and getting your credentials, refer [here](https://www.moengage.com/docs/api/introduction#getting-your-credentials).

CampaignStatsRequest.description: Request body to fetch campaign stats.

request_id.description: This field shows the request ID created by a user. Helps to know the API calls made by the client.

campaign_ids.description: This field shows the campaign IDs created, up to 10 max per call.

start_date.description: This field shows the start date of the campaign in YYYY-MM-DD format. This date is interpreted in your MoEngage account's app timezone.

end_date.description: This field shows the campaign's end date in YYYY-MM-DD format. The days between the start and end dates should not exceed 30 days. This date is interpreted in your MoEngage account's app timezone.

attribution_type.description: This field shows the attribution type that should be picked to show conversion stats.

offset.description:
This field shows the position of a record in a dataset. 
The default value for the number of campaigns to skip is 0. 
For example, setting the offset to 50 skips the first 50 records. The resulting page number depends on your limit. With a limit of 10, an offset of 50 returns page 6.

limit.description: This field shows the maximum number of campaigns displayed on a page. The default and max limit is up to 10 campaigns.

metric_type.description: This field shows the total or unique values of all the metrics.

response_id.description: The response ID, which is the same as the request ID passed in the payload.

total_campaigns.description: This field indicates the total number of campaigns that are requested in the payload.

current_page.description: This field indicates the current page number.

total_pages.description: This field indicates the total page. It is equal to the total campaigns, which is limited to 10 for each call and 10 to be displayed for each page.

data.description: This object contains the campaign stats. Keys are Campaign IDs.

Platforms.description: This field indicates the platforms where the user has engaged with your communication (e.g., ANDROID, IOS, WEB, MWEB, UNKNOWN).

Locales.description: This field indicates the details of the locales configured.

Variations.description: This object contains details of the variations of your locale.

PerformanceStats.description: This object shows your campaign's performance metrics.

failed.description: Number of communications that failed to reach customers.

impression.description: Number of times your communication appeared to the user.

click.description: Number of times your users clicked the message.

opened.description: Number of communications opened by the user.

delivered.description: Number of communications delivered to the customer.

read.description: Number of customers who read your communications.

closed_click.description: Number of messages closed by your customers.

unsubscribe.description: Number of customers who have unsubscribed.

ConversionGoalStats.description: This object shows the conversion goal stats of your campaign.

DeliveryFunnel.description: This object shows the delivery stats of your campaign.

FailureBreakdown.description: This object shows the failure breakdown of your campaign.
